reason: A gate change by the agent that commits to the repository is normally not acceptable, but this one rests on Dinis's own words, which I found exactly, and it tightens as well as extends. It lets a key be filed under the full agent id where the short name is taken (here cl-6.conductor.json already belongs to cl-6.conductor@sgit.dinis), and it adds a guard the old code lacked: self-publication is refused when that agent already has a live key in the repository, so a second file cannot slip a second key in under an existing identity. Unchanged: a commit still cannot vouch for itself with any other change, keys are read from the first parent, and a site cannot claim a Factory identity held with another key. The recycled conductor's first commit (site/keys/cl-6.conductor@SovereignWebsite.dinis.json alone) will pass, because that agent has no key here yet.

findings.finding: Agent ids are matched case-sensitively (k.agent === agent), while the agent pattern accepts any case and the file pattern now allows capitals. A case variant of an existing agent (for example a lower-case @sovereignwebsite.dinis) counts as a new agent with no live key and could self-publish.
findings.condition: Compare agent ids in lower case for the live-key guard, and refuse a self-publication whose id equals an existing agent's id in any case. Small enough to fold into the Factory patch before Org apply.

findings.finding: The new guard also means an agent whose key here is still live cannot self-publish a replacement; the old file must be marked superseded or retired first (by a signed commit of a person or of a key that counts). That is the safer behaviour; restart.md files should say so.

conditions: Finding 1 fixed in the Factory patch, and in this repository at the next change of the file.
